Q: How to efficiently denormalize a SQL DB to produce Parquet files A:

What's worked for me is streaming chunks through PyArrow instead of loading everything at once:

import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import pandas as pd

engine = sqlalchemy.create_engine('postgresql://...')
query = '''
    SELECT o.*, c.name as customer_name, p.title
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
    JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id
'''

writer = None
for chunk_df in pd.read_sql(query, engine, chunksize=50000):
    table = pa.Table.from_pandas(chunk_df)
    if writer is None:
        writer = pq.ParquetWriter('output.parquet', table.schema,
                                   compression='snappy')
    writer.write_table(table)
writer.close()

This way you never hold the whole denormalized dataset in memory. Snappy compression is a good default -- fast and decent compression ratio.

Q: ASP.NET Web API: Non-descriptive 500 Internal Server Error A:

This Scenario was caused for the following reasons

  1. The problem occurred due to misformed Web.config. ( Multiple configSections)

  2. Instead of creating roslyn folder inside bin folder, I had it created at the root. (Deployment location.)

The best way to diagnose this was, to put a simple HTML page at the application location and try to browse it. 500 Error description will be displayed on this html page.

And also don't forget to add

<customErrors mode="Off"></customErrors>

to Web.config

Q: How can I install faiss-gpu? A:

Try this:

  • Go to https://pypi.org/project/faiss-gpu-cu12/#history

  • Select and copy the correct package name from the pypi

  • try pip install again

This will work. Error is occuring because pypi package name for faiss-gpu is not longer 'faiss-gpu'.
